d6_d8_two_face_test: Registered D6 front/solder corners project the front pair to roughly (1788,1053)/(1781,1267) in solder tile 200527310. A separate inter-package x fit from D8.8 to D6.1 shifts the search to roughly x1782/1775; these ≈6 px different estimates show the extrapolation uncertainty. Native solder crop (1580,970)-(1930,1330) shows a joint near (1767,1055), about 15–21 px from the upper projections, with a short uninterrupted B.Cu trace to registered D6.1 near (1850,1055). D6.1 is the modeled A6 address input, not +5 V or ground. The lower projection falls on/near a separate broad tinned strip, without a distinct confirmed same-hole joint. If the front upper candidate is solder joint (1767,1055), it is a D6.1 signal node and cannot be a source-drawn C86 bypass pad. This package-only extrapolation initially left a 15–21 px x residual; the independent gap fiducial below resolves that local offset.
gap_local_fiducial_correction: Native front crop (1800,1120)-(2100,1620) resolves a distinct open annulus near (1963,1235), directly above the filled/wired upper front candidate near (1960,1315). Native solder crop (1650,830)-(1950,1060) resolves an open annulus near (1767,973), directly above the soldered joint (1767,1055) on the short D6.1 B.Cu branch. The paired vertical geometry and independent open drill make the front upper joint→solder (1767,1055) match substantially stronger than package-only extrapolation. The front copper has a visible brown gap to D6.1 at the socket edge, consistent with the connection being on the solder face. Owner meter continuity remains the definitive check.
remaining_gap_inventory: Exact assembly crop (1500,250)-(2700,1350) draws C86 at D6/D8 package height, with a vertical body and leads, so the tempting front (1960,1315)/(1967,1533) pair fits its geometry but fails the bypass-net test. Native component crop (1800,1120)-(2100,1620) shows three other open upper annuli around (1935,1155), (1990,1182), and (1963,1235), above the socket tops. The first two terminate separate narrow front traces; the last aligns with the short green wire into the upper joint and is the local registration fiducial on the D6.1 branch. The only conspicuous lower gap joint is near (1967,1533), visibly separated from the wired upper broad strip. No second rail-identified vertical pair is resolved in this photographed gap. An unseen solder-covered drill or F.Cu route remains possible, so this is a negative photo inventory rather than evidence that factory C86 was DNP.
electrical_boundary: Exact .009 sheet 1 groups C86 with C82–C93 as +5 V-to-ground bypasses. The assembly position alone does not identify which owner-board holes, if any, implement that pair.
conclusion: Exclude the leading vertical front pair as the C86 +5 V/GND bypass candidate: its upper wired joint is locally photo-registered to solder (1767,1055), visibly routed to D6.1/A6. This is a photo-based exclusion, pending owner continuity confirmation. The actual C86 pad pair, value, and population remain open; do not assign the other upper open annuli or the single broad run by proximity.
next_inspection: With power off, confirm front upper joint (1960,1315) to solder joint (1767,1055) and physical D6.1/A6; test the independent open-hole fiducial pair (1963,1235)/(1767,973) to verify the local face registration.
